decisions.what: Confirm GAL's MoU status and scope with Embraer, and open contact with Generation 5 Holding.
Confirm GAL's UAS positioning and request meetings with Calidus and EDGE.
Open dialogue with EDGE business development on where in-country support and training would sit.

priorities.name: Embraer C-390 sustainment and training
priorities.next: Agree sustainment and training scope, or a teaming position with Generation 5; track the Saudi C-390 versus C-130J decision.
priorities.now: Confirm GAL MoU status and scope with Embraer; name an internal lead; open contact with Generation 5 Holding.
priorities.why: Tawazun contracted 10 C-390s (options for 10 more) in May 2026. Embraer made Generation 5 Holding its exclusive UAE partner for MRO, support and training; reports do not mention GAL or AMMROC. GAL remains a named partner in the Nov 2025 MoU. No new facts this week.

priorities.name: UAS sustainment and training role
priorities.next: Draft a sustainment and training teaming proposal.
priorities.now: Confirm GAL UAS positioning; request meetings with Calidus and EDGE.
priorities.why: The MQ-9B/Gambit co-production MOU between General Atomics and Calidus creates local support needs. EDGE bundles long-term support into export UAS-related deals (Morocco, 9 Oct), which suggests a similar model at home. No new UAE facts this week.

priorities.name: EDGE-Hanwha air defense support
priorities.next: Position for JV support scope once a definitive agreement is signed.
priorities.now: Open dialogue with EDGE business development on where in-country support and training would sit.
priorities.why: The 15 September term sheet covers L-SAM, M-SAM and Chunmoo with phased localisation. A joint venture is only to be pursued, subject to government approvals, and the reports do not mention sustainment or training. Support demand is probable but not yet defined, and the timing depends on a definitive agreement.

summary: No new UAE or GCC sustainment, MRO, manpower, training, UAS, tanker or firefighting development naming GAL or a watchlist company was verified for 6 to 13 November. Searches on EDGE, Embraer and Generation 5, AMMROC, General Atomics and Calidus, AAR, Serco, Hanwha, GE Aerospace, Boeing, Lockheed Martin, Gulf sustainment, tankers and aerial firefighting returned only items already on file or older material. No items were added. The three standing priorities are unchanged, and the Embraer C-390 decision date is today, 13 November.
